card.title: 43e RÉGIMENT MOTORISÉ
card.text: When this unit loses Mobilize, fully repair your units.
card.flavorText: The 43rd Infantry Regiment was a unit of the French Army that was active from 1638 to 2010. It was originally created as the Régiment Royal des Vaisseaux, a regiment that was set to serve on ships and in the colonies, hence its name, meaning The Royal Regiment of Vessels. It was the first marine troops regiment in the French army. During WWI, the regiment fought relentlessly on all major battlefields (the Marne, the Somme, Verdun, etc.) for 4 years. In 1939 the regiment became part of the 1st Motorized Infantry Division and was redesignated as the 43rd Motorized Infantry Regiment, a unit comprising 3000 men. During the "Phoney war" it was stationed in Oise in Northern France, up until May 1940 when it was sent to Belgium where it participated in heavy fighting against the German forces. Despite fierce resistance the regiment experienced heavy casualties and was forced to retreat to Lille, and later to Dunkirk where they continued the fight but were ordered to lay down arms after losing 231 killed and 600 wounded. After the Armistice was signed, the regiment was redesignated 43rd Alpine Infantry Regiment and was stationed in Marseille and Digne, but in 1942 it was disbanded. In 1945 the regiment was restored and would later participate in the Indochina War (1947-1948) and the Algerian War (1956-1962). In 2010 the 43rd Infantry Regiment was disbanded.
